paragraphs: Dudley Council runs its own fostering service, Fostering in Dudley, and children from the borough also live with independent agencies such as those shown above. During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2026 the council said more than 500 children were in care across the borough and that it had nearly 80 foster carers. It asked for at least 60 more people to come forward, to meet growing demand and so that children can stay in their own communities, close to their schools, friends and support networks.

The council is clear that you do not need to own your home or live in a traditional family to foster, and it welcomes people from all backgrounds. Its carers receive full training and financial support, and Fostering in Dudley offers support 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. You can reach the team through fosteringindudley.org.uk or on 01384 815833.

Dudley also works with its neighbours. It is one of the four councils, with Sandwell, Walsall and Wolverhampton, behind Black Country Fostering, a regional hub that the government named as one of four new fostering hubs in England. The hub gives people thinking about fostering one place to go for information and advice, runs an ambassador scheme so you can talk to experienced carers before you apply, and offers training and support to carers already fostering (blackcountryfostering.org.uk, 0800 923 3706). It is part of a national aim of 10,000 more fostering places.

Choosing between the council and an agency is mostly about the support and the kind of fostering you want. Fostering for Dudley means working with the team responsible for the borough's children, and the council's recent appeal is about keeping those children local. An agency recruits, trains and supports its own carers and takes referrals from councils, Dudley among them.

If you live in the borough, ask the council and two or three of the agencies above the same questions: what they pay, what training comes before and after approval, how often a supervising social worker visits, and who answers the phone at night.
